cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Change What the Apology Is For
cards.instruction: Get an apology, then reveal that the original offense was only the first layer of what needs repair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I accept your apology for breaking my vase. Now tell me when you knew the dog hadn't done it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Straight away. I'll buy you another vase.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep your money. You watched me shut the dog out of this room for three days. That is the part you're going to put right.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was embarrassed to admit it. Shall I let him back in?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. Call him in. Then apologise to me for leaving me to punish him. Your embarrassment stopped you speaking; mine began when I found out who I'd believed.

reason: Remove the unsupported confiscated bed; use B offered room-access repair and distinguish B initial embarrassment from A later shame over misdirected punishment.
